title: Sounds and greetings
description: Unit 0 check after lessons 1 and 2: hear the sounds, greet people at the right time.

items.question: Which word did you hear?
items.explanation: z is 'ts' (Zeit, time). s before a vowel is a soft z sound (seit, since).

items.question: Which word did you hear?
items.explanation: ie is a long ee: Wien (Vienna). ei sounds like 'eye': Wein (wine).

items.question: Which word did you hear?
items.explanation: ü is i with rounded lips: Tür (door). Tier (animal) has a plain long ee.
Guten Morgen: both words start with a capital letter here.
Ihnen (polite 'you') always has a capital I.

items.question: It's 8 pm and you walk into a restaurant. What do you say?
items.explanation: Guten Abend to greet in the evening; Gute Nacht only when someone goes to bed.

items.question: Your friend is leaving the party. What do you say?
items.explanation: Tschüss = bye (informal). With a stranger or an official: Auf Wiedersehen.
Wie geht es dir? is the full informal form; Wie geht's? is the short one.

items.text: Guten Tag! Wie geht es Ihnen? - Sehr gut, danke. Und ___?
items.explanation: Answer in the same form: Wie geht es Ihnen? - Und Ihnen?

items.instruction: Write a short exchange (3-4 lines) between you and a new colleague in the morning: greet them, ask how they are, answer, and say goodbye. Use du or Sie, but stay consistent. Claude will check it.
items.prompt: Morning, new colleague: greet, ask how they are, answer, say goodbye.
